correctness.rationale: The exact half-line sine kernel and independent block rate-Laplace factors yield the finite-time survival identity. Low-frequency concentration gives the correct Gamma prefactor and fixed-phase ratio; monotonicity in phase upgrades pointwise convergence to a uniform limit. The signed sine spectral measure is handled correctly: the fractional Bernstein representation proves strict positivity of every cusp coefficient, and the Laplace-derivative bound proves a finite left derivative. The asymptotic normalized cusp coefficient is the same Gamma ratio. Boundary alpha=1 and theta=0,1 were checked. An independent checker passed 193 finite assertions for several rate-law transforms and positions, but the analytic argument is the basis of the infinite statements.

evidence: The 2024 supplement proves finite jumps of a bounded-domain first-passage density for exponentially distributed rates, which corresponds to alpha=1 rather than the infinite-mean fractional cusp (https://journals.aps.org/prresearch/supplemental/10.1103/PhysRevResearch.6.L012033/SM.pdf).

Finite-size rounding gives a mean-passage crossover in a reflecting finite chain, not a surviving half-line particle phase fingerprint (https://github.com/published-finding corpus/2026/tree/main/2026/11/8/SCOPE-finite-size-rounding-of-a-fluctuating-rate-first-passage-transit--4aa761bb0923).

The initiating paper proves only the exact survival kernel, leading power law and mean transition; prior finite-mean discontinuity calculations, long-distance scaling, finite-size means and bounded-rate survival comparisons do not establish the fractional phase law. value.rationale: The theorem isolates a universal measurable within-period first-passage effect, not visible in the known leading survival tail, and proves that the heavy-tail index can be identified from one normalized interior phase in the ideal asymptotic regime. It gives a strict heavy-tail versus finite-mean dichotomy at the first relative order, a fractional singularity at every redraw, and the exact decay of its positive coefficient. The problem is motivated by documented density discontinuities in periodic rate refreshes and a recent half-line mean-time transition. The result is a structural universality statement, not a finite arbitrary table or a bare restatement of the source integral. Noise robustness and randomized schedules remain open.
